design.quote: double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover design in 22 healthy participants (11 women, 11 men) who received placebo and DMT (0.6, 1.2, 1.8, and 2.4 mg/min) over an infusion duration of 120 min
design.text: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover study in 22 healthy participants

findings.quote: The present study documented the presence of acute pharmacological tolerance to the continuous administration of DMT.
findings.text: The study documented that acute pharmacological tolerance occurs with the continuous administration of DMT.

findings.quote: We observed moderate acute tolerance to subjective effects of DMT, indicated by clockwise hysteresis (Fig.). Specifically, subjective effects showed no increase from 30 to 120 min, despite increasing plasma concentrations.
findings.text: Moderate acute tolerance to the subjective effects of DMT was observed, as subjective effects did not increase from 30 to 120 min despite increasing plasma concentrations.

findings.quote: Our findings and others do not support the view that DMT exerts no tolerance, in contrast to other psychedelics.
findings.text: The findings of this study and others do not support the view that DMT exerts no tolerance.

limits.quote: Self-titration occurred in participants with recent DMT experience and would need to be replicated in non-experienced individuals.
limits.text: Self-titration results occurred in participants with recent DMT experience and need to be replicated in individuals without experience.

ref.title: Psychological and physiological effects of extended DMT

sources.title: Psychological and physiological effects of extended DMT

findings.quote: The increase in plasma levels of DMT from minutes 10 to 30, while subjective effects remain sustained suggest the development of short-term psychological tolerance induced by DMT.
findings.text: Short-term psychological tolerance to DMT appears to develop during continuous infusion.

findings.quote: These findings may suggest a progressive development of acute psychological tolerance to DMT during continuous infusion, a finding not seen in previous studies employing this compound.
findings.text: Acute psychological tolerance to DMT may progressively develop during continuous infusion.

limits.quote: the observed variability between individuals makes it difficult to draw any final conclusions based on this analysis.
limits.text: Individual variability makes it difficult to draw definitive conclusions about short-term tolerance.
